styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Intramuros walls, Fort Santiago and Rizal's story.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Binondo noodle houses and sizzling Filipino plates.

styles.label: Shopping
styles.blurb: Malls in Makati and bargain hunting in Divisoria.

stays.why: Walk to Rizal Park and the Intramuros gates; LRT Line 1 stops nearby. Good mix of budget and mid-range hotels.
Cheaper rooms, cafés and bars, and a short walk to the baywalk. LRT Line 1 runs through it.
Sleep inside the old walled city, steps from Fort Santiago and the churches. Quiet at night, few rooms.
Modern business district with the best malls and restaurants; more polished but farther from the old sights.

food: Eat adobo, sinigang (sour soup) and lechon; a casual meal runs about PHP 150–350.
Binondo is the place for Chinese-Filipino food: noodles, dumplings and hopia pastries. Go hungry and share plates.
Try a halo-halo for dessert and a sizzling sisig with rice for a cheap, filling dinner.
Street food is everywhere: grilled skewers and fishballs. Pick busy stalls and eat food cooked hot in front of you.
Book ahead at popular restaurants on weekends; mall food courts are a cheap, safe fallback for first-timers.
more_time: Add a day trip to Tagaytay for cooler air and volcano views; check travel time on the day, traffic is heavy.
Swap one city day for a ferry or drive to Corregidor Island for WWII history; book tours in advance.
Spend a morning in Quiapo and Santa Cruz markets for cheap finds and local life along LRT Line 1.

recommend.why: Two nights cover Intramuros, Rizal Park and a Binondo food crawl; add a night if you want Makati malls or a day trip.

month_notes: January: dry and mild, highs near 29°C. Great for walking Intramuros.
February: the driest month, about 6 rain days. Book outdoor plans now.
March: warmer at 32°C with few showers. Start early to beat the heat.
April: hot at 33°C and still fairly dry. Carry water and plan shade breaks.
May: rains arrive, about 18 rain days. Keep indoor backups ready.
June: wet season, around 26 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
July: wettest stretch, about 28 rain days. Pack a rain jacket and flexible plans.
August: still very wet, around 28 rain days. Flooding is possible; check routes on the day.
September: rain continues, about 28 rain days. Malls and museums are good rainy-day picks.
October: still wet at about 25 rain days, but showers start to ease.
November: rain drops to about 15 days. Comfortable for sightseeing again.
December: mild at 30°C with about 15 rain days. Busy holiday season, book hotels early.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, with a clear dry season from January to April and a long wet season from May to October.

items.title: Best time: January to April
items.text: Highs of 29–33°C and the fewest rain days, from 6 to 10 a month. Best for walking the old city.

items.title: Wet season: June to October
items.text: Rain on 25–28 days a month. Showers are often heavy and short; plan indoor stops and check roads on the day.

items.title: Hot and humid year-round
items.text: Lows stay around 23–26°C, so nights are warm. April is the hottest month at 33°C highs.

items.title: Carry rain gear in the wet months
items.text: A light rain jacket or umbrella helps from May to October. Streets can flood briefly after heavy rain.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Storms are most likely from June to November. Check forecasts before day trips and keep plans flexible.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light, breathable clothes, sunscreen and a hat; a rain layer for the wet months; comfortable shoes for uneven old-city streets.

transit.best: LRT Line 1 for the old sights, plus ride apps for everything else.

modes.text: LRT Line 1 (green) links Malate, Ermita, Quiapo, Binondo and Santa Cruz, where most sights sit. LRT Line 2 (blue) serves Quiapo, Sampaloc and Santa Mesa; trains are packed at rush hour.
City buses start around PHP 16 and provincial buses around PHP 12. Route numbers are shown on the bus.
Grab, Angkas, Gojek, Joyride and MyTaxi.PH work. Taxis are plentiful but insist on the meter.
Not recommended for first-timers: heavy traffic and hard parking. Use apps and rail instead.
Good inside Intramuros and around Rizal Park. Sidewalks are uneven and hot at midday; cross with care.
From about PHP 10 for the first 4 km. Routes are painted on the sides, not numbered, so ask the driver.
Short trips only. A one-hour calesa ride in the old city costs around PHP 50–70; agree the price first.
